recentItems.title: Attacks on schools are their new ‘victory’: Podolyak on Moscow’s barbaric tactics
recentItems.description:
Why is Putin threatening Europe, and what lies behind the intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities? Mykhailo Podolyak explains how Russia targets schools, hospitals, and scientific institutions to compensate for the lack of success on the front line. In this interview — strikes on Kyiv and a school in Sumy, the significance of attacks on Russian oil refineries, and the danger of negotiations on Kremlin terms. We discuss joint weapons production, sanctions, pressure on China, and Russian sabotage operations in Europe. Why statements fail to deter the aggressor, how Moscow interferes in elections, and why war participants can still travel to the EU? An analysis of threats and solutions for Ukraine and its partners.

recentItems.title: Putin admits a 1% loss in GDP at the Valdai Forum! Gasoline in Russia now rationed by license plate
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian drones delivered ground robots behind enemy lines to strike Russian positions. On the Lyman axis, Operation "Vivaldi" reclaimed 176 km² for Ukraine: according to the 3rd Army Corps, over 250 occupiers surrendered. Strikes on six Russian oil refineries exacerbate a fuel crisis as the Kremlin classifies petroleum industry data. In this issue: the first combat use of the FP-7, a Tu-95MS crash, the interception of a "Geran-4," and new military aid for Ukrainian air defense. We also break down F-16 deliveries from Belgium, UK support, and Moscow's nuclear threats involving Kaliningrad.

recentItems.title: False-flag operation: The Kremlin is preparing to ATTACK ITSELF
recentItems.description:
The Kremlin is issuing nuclear threats once again — this time over Kaliningrad. At the Valdai Club, Putin declared Russia's readiness to deploy all available forces, while NATO reinforces the defense of its eastern flank. Why has the Suwalki Gap become a major flashpoint, and could Moscow stage a provocation to justify a new wave of mobilization? We break down Radosław Sikorski's warnings, acts of sabotage, and hybrid attacks in Europe, as well as shifts in Russia's nuclear doctrine. Mark Rutte and Matthew Whitaker emphasize: the Alliance stands ready to defend its territory. How are Ukraine's partners responding to this blackmail, and why is the Kremlin trying to intimidate the West to undermine support for Kyiv?

recentItems.title: "PUTIN'S HALLUCINATIONS": ISW shreds Kremlin tales of front-line "breakthrough"
recentItems.description:
Russia targets Kyiv's bridges, residential areas of Kharkiv and Izium, while FPV drones hunt transport and civilians in Zaporizhzhia. Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a drone base in Donetsk and military facilities in the Belgorod region. This episode covers the aftermath of the shelling, air defense operations, city defenses against drones, and the humanitarian disaster in occupied Oleshky. We also discuss Russian airborne threats to Europe, NATO's response, new Japanese sanctions, and US investments in Ukrainian mineral resources. ISW analysts refute Putin's claims of battlefield successes: according to their data, Russia lost over 80 square kilometers of territory in September.

Ukrainian long-range strikes target oil refineries and missile-manufacturing facilities. Meanwhile, Ukrainian intelligence has obtained documents detailing Russia's preparations for winter attacks on the energy grid. How is Ukraine protecting critical facilities?
